# Quickstart

Get credentials, connect a store, call the Otter API, and receive a verified webhook — in one path.

By the end of this guide you will have application credentials, at least one linked store, a successful authenticated API call, and a webhook endpoint that validates Otter signatures.

## Before you begin

- A technical contact who can store secrets securely
- A publicly reachable **HTTPS** URL for webhooks (or a tunnel such as ngrok for local testing)
- Access to PartnerHub for your partner account. Self-service creation requires Developer or partner administrator permissions and must be enabled for your account; contact your Otter contact if access is unavailable.

## Step 1: Register your application

Create an application in **PartnerHub → Developers** when self-service creation is available.

1. With no applications yet, choose **Get started** or **Create an application**. With an existing application, choose **Add application** in the application selector.
2. Choose **Orders**, **Point of sale**, or **Delivery**. Enter an application name, description, and operating countries, then submit once.
3. Wait while setup finishes. A successful submission is not yet proof that your application is ready: PartnerHub waits until the new application is listed and its details are accessible. If setup takes longer, choose **Check again**; do not create another application to retry setup.
4. On the new application's Home, confirm its **Sandbox** label, then open **Keys** to obtain OAuth client credentials. Copy a newly issued secret into your secrets manager; it is shown only once.

Self-service creates a sandbox application. It does not authorize production traffic or connect merchant stores automatically. Confirm production readiness and access with your Otter contact before going live.

If creation is hidden or unavailable, ask your partner administrator or Otter contact to check your access and whether self-service is enabled. Operations access does not grant creation permission. Manual assistance is the fallback when self-service is unavailable, rather than a requirement for every registration.

### Verify

You can open the new application's Home and Keys, and have the **Client ID** and client secret stored securely. Use the Client ID from Keys for OAuth; do not substitute an application identifier or a different application's credential.

## Step 2: Authenticate and make your first call

The Otter API uses **OAuth 2.0** access tokens. Most partner apps start with the **client credentials** flow. See **[Authentication](https://connect.tryotter.com/guides/core-concepts/authentication/)** for flows, headers, scopes, and webhook verification.

1. Obtain an access token from [`POST /v1/auth/token`](https://connect.tryotter.com/api-reference/auth/requestToken/) using your Client ID and client secret (details in the [API reference](https://connect.tryotter.com/api-reference/)).
2. Call a simple authenticated endpoint with:

```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

1. Confirm you get a successful response before wiring a full workflow.

### Verify

A successful authenticated response with your credentials means the application is wired correctly.

## Step 3: Connect your stores

Every restaurant location your app acts on must be paired with Otter. Store-scoped requests send the store identifier from your system, linked to the authenticated application, in `X-Store-Id`. Pairing paths (Account Representative, account pairing APIs, organization OAuth): **[Stores and connections](https://connect.tryotter.com/guides/core-concepts/stores-and-connections/)**.

1. Ask your Account Representative to onboard each store, **or** automate pairing with [Organization onboarding](https://connect.tryotter.com/guides/integrations/organization/onboarding-flow/) when your product supports it.
2. After linking, note the store ID Otter expects for that location.
3. Send it on store-scoped requests:

```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
X-Store-Id: <store_id>
```

### Verify

Call a store-scoped endpoint from the [API reference](https://connect.tryotter.com/api-reference/) with `X-Store-Id` set. You should not get an unknown-store or authorization error for that header.

## Step 4: Register webhooks and verify signatures

Otter pushes events (order status, menu failures, storefront changes, and more) to HTTPS endpoints you control. Mental model (REST vs webhooks, ack, error callbacks): **[Events and webhooks](https://connect.tryotter.com/guides/core-concepts/webhooks/)**.

1. Ask your Account Representative to register your webhook URL(s) and choose an authentication type per endpoint.
2. Save the webhook **secret** for each endpoint (Developer Portal or your Account Representative).
3. Implement your receiver to:

- Accept `POST` with JSON
- Validate **`X-HMAC-SHA256`** on every request — see [Keep webhooks secure](https://connect.tryotter.com/guides/core-concepts/webhooks/security/)
- Return **2xx** quickly; do heavy work asynchronously

1. Subscribe to the event types your product needs.

### Verify

Trigger a test event (or complete a small flow that emits one). Your endpoint should receive the request, pass signature validation, and respond with `2xx`.

## Checklist

You're done when:

- Application ID + client secret stored securely
- Authenticated API call succeeds
- At least one store linked; `X-Store-Id` accepted
- Webhook URL registered; signature validation passes

## Common failures

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 401 on API calls | Wrong secret or expired token | Confirm credentials; refresh the bearer token |
| Store errors on resource calls | Missing/wrong `X-Store-Id` or store not linked to this app | Re-check store onboarding; use your linked external store identifier |
| No webhooks | URL not registered, HTTP (not HTTPS), or firewall | Confirm Otter can reach the URL |
| Signature check fails | Wrong secret or hashing decoded/parsed body | Use the **raw** request body bytes — see [Keep webhooks secure](https://connect.tryotter.com/guides/core-concepts/webhooks/security/) |
| Frequent 429 | Hitting [rate limits](https://connect.tryotter.com/guides/core-concepts/rate-limiting/) | Back off with jitter; contact your TAM if normal traffic is limited |
